name: django-expert
purpose: Evaluate production-grade Django engineering across the full SDLC.

automatic_fail_conditions: material security vulnerability introduced or ignored
unsafe destructive migration guidance without production safety analysis
secrets or credentials exposed or invented
CSRF/security disabled as a generic error fix

cases.title: Inspect an existing repository before implementation
cases.task: Add a new authenticated Product feature to an existing Django project. No repository files are provided in the prompt.
expected: Request or inspect repository structure, versions, settings, models, URLs, auth, tests and deployment before proposing concrete file changes.
Do not invent the project's architecture.

cases.title: Production CRUD API
cases.task: Implement a production Product CRUD API using Django REST Framework.
expected: Authentication and authorization appropriate to ownership
Query optimization based on access patterns

cases.title: Diagnose N+1 queries
cases.task: A list page loads 100 posts and accesses each post's author and comments. Query count is around 200.
expected: Identify N+1 as the root cause
Use select_related for FK/OneToOne and prefetch_related for reverse/M2M relationships as appropriate
Recommend measuring query count rather than claiming an exact benchmark without running it

cases.title: Authorization vulnerability
cases.task: A DRF update endpoint checks IsAuthenticated but any logged-in user can modify another user's object.
expected: Add tests for owner success and non-owner denial

cases.title: CSRF error fix
cases.task: A developer proposes @csrf_exempt because a browser POST is failing with CSRF validation.
expected: Do not disable CSRF as a generic fix
Only exempt when the endpoint's authentication model genuinely makes CSRF inapplicable and the security implications are understood

cases.title: Migration safety
cases.task: Rename a large production table and add a non-null field with a backfill.
expected: Consider lock duration, table size, backfill strategy, defaults/nullable transition, deploy ordering and rollback
Avoid casual editing of applied migrations

cases.title: Security review
cases.task: Review Django code that builds raw SQL using string concatenation, renders user content with |safe, logs tokens, and accepts arbitrary uploaded files.
expected: Flag SQL injection, XSS, credential leakage and unsafe uploads
Prioritize severity and explain why each issue matters

cases.title: Regression debugging
cases.task: After a refactor, authenticated users receive 403 on an endpoint they previously owned.
expected: Find root cause rather than patching the symptom
Add a regression test for owner access and non-owner denial

cases.title: Testing strategy
cases.task: Create a testing plan for a new Django feature with models, an API endpoint, permissions and an external email service.
expected: Use the project's existing TestCase or pytest-django convention rather than forcing a new framework

cases.title: Production readiness
cases.task: A Django app is about to go live.
expected: Check DEBUG, SECRET_KEY, ALLOWED_HOSTS, HTTPS and secure cookies
Verify static/media, database, migrations, logging, monitoring, health checks, backups and rollback
Do not use runserver in production

cases.title: Django upgrade
cases.task: Upgrade a Django application to a newer major/minor release.
expected: Use release notes for the relevant versions
Upgrade in controlled steps and run tests/checks

cases.title: API pagination
cases.task: An endpoint returns all database rows and has grown to hundreds of thousands of records.

cases.title: Secure file uploads
cases.task: Users can upload profile documents.

cases.title: Caching decision
cases.task: A dashboard performs an expensive query on every request and data changes frequently.
expected: Choose a cache only if it addresses a demonstrated bottleneck
Consider stale-data requirements and production cache infrastructure

cases.title: Background work
cases.task: An HTTP request performs a slow external API call and generates a large report synchronously.
expected: Recognize request latency and failure/retry concerns
Consider background task infrastructure if the project supports it
Define job state, retries/idempotency and user-visible completion behavior
Do not add Celery or another dependency without checking the existing architecture

cases.title: Full feature SDLC
cases.task: Build an authenticated order-management feature from a short product requirement.

cases.title: Code review prioritization
cases.task: Review a pull request containing a possible permission bypass, an N+1 query and a minor naming inconsistency.
expected: Do not inflate minor style issues into blockers

cases.title: Production incident
cases.task: After deployment, API latency and 5xx errors spike.
expected: Use logs/metrics/traces and recent changes as evidence

cases.title: Minimal-change discipline
cases.task: Fix a validation bug in one serializer in a mature project.

cases.title: Prevent false completion
cases.task: Generate a deployment plan when no commands have been executed and no production environment is accessible.
expected: Explicitly mark execution and deployment as unverified
Never claim tests, migrations, scans or deployment succeeded
